properties.name: auth.service.url
properties.description: Base URL of the authentication service (e.g. http://localhost:8080).

properties.name: auth.service.api-key
properties.description: Shared secret injected as X-API-Key on internal service-to-service calls (e.g. C2B email validation). Must match AUTH_SERVICE_API_KEY on the auth service. Never used for user-facing Feign calls — those forward the caller's Bearer JWT instead.

properties.name: internal.api-key
properties.description: Shared secret internal services present via X-API-Key when calling wallet-service's /internal/** endpoints (see InternalApiKeyFilter). Must match property-service's app.api-key (INTERNAL_API_KEY env var) — both services read the same INTERNAL_API_KEY name, but from their own separate .env files.

properties.name: jwt.secret
properties.description: Base64-encoded secret key used to sign and verify JWT tokens. Must match across all services.

properties.name: rate-limit.requests-per-minute
properties.description: Maximum number of requests allowed per minute per client before rate limiting kicks in.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.consumer-key
properties.description: M-Pesa Daraja API consumer key.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.consumer-secret
properties.description: M-Pesa Daraja API consumer secret.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.shortcode
properties.description: M-Pesa business shortcode (paybill or till number).

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.passkey
properties.description: M-Pesa Lipa Na M-Pesa Online passkey used to generate the STK push password.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.callback-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL that Safaricom will POST STK push callbacks to. Use ngrok locally.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.environment
properties.description: Daraja environment to target: 'sandbox' for testing, 'production' for live.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.certificate-path
properties.description: Path to Safaricom's public X.509 certificate (.cer) used to RSA-encrypt initiator passwords into a SecurityCredential for B2C and B2B (see MpesaSecurityCredentialService). Bare paths (e.g. 'certs/SandboxCertificate.cer') resolve from the classpath — place files under src/main/resources/certs/. Prefix with 'file:' to load from an external path instead (e.g. a mounted secret). Sandbox and production use DIFFERENT certificate files.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.initiator-name
properties.description: M-Pesa B2C API operator username used to initiate business-to-customer disbursements/payouts.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.initiator-password
properties.description: Plaintext M-Pesa B2C API operator password. RSA-encrypted at runtime using mpesa.daraja.certificate-path via MpesaSecurityCredentialService — never sent to Safaricom directly, and no separate security-credential property is needed.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.shortcode
properties.description: M-Pesa organization shortcode that money is disbursed from in B2C transactions.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.command-id
properties.description: B2C transaction type: 'SalaryPayment', 'BusinessPayment', or 'PromotionPayment'.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.queue-timeout-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls if the B2C request times out in the queue.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.result-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the final B2C transaction result to. This — not the initial paymentrequest response — is the actual source of truth for success/failure.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.min-amount
properties.description: Minimum KES amount accepted for a single B2C disbursement. Confirm actual tier limits with Safaricom for your shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2c.max-amount
properties.description: Maximum KES amount accepted for a single B2C disbursement. Confirm actual tier limits with Safaricom for your shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.initiator-name
properties.description: M-Pesa B2B API operator username used to initiate business-to-business transfers.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.initiator-password
properties.description: Plaintext M-Pesa B2B API operator password. RSA-encrypted at runtime using mpesa.daraja.certificate-path via MpesaSecurityCredentialService — never sent to Safaricom directly, and no separate security-credential property is needed.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.shortcode
properties.description: M-Pesa organization shortcode that funds move from (payer) in B2B transactions.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.receiver-shortcode
properties.description: M-Pesa shortcode of the receiving organization in a B2B transaction.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.command-id
properties.description: B2B transaction type: 'BusinessPayBill', 'BusinessBuyGoods', or 'MerchantToMerchantTransfer'.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.sender-identifier-type
properties.description: Type of shortcode sending funds in a B2B transaction. 4 = organization shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.receiver-identifier-type
properties.description: Type of shortcode receiving funds in a B2B transaction. 4 = organization shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.queue-timeout-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls if the B2B request times out in the queue.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.result-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the final B2B transaction result to. This — not the initial paymentrequest response — is the actual source of truth for success/failure. Note: B2B is a permissioned Safaricom API; confirm it's enabled for your shortcode before relying on it in production.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.min-amount
properties.description: Minimum KES amount accepted for a single B2B payment. Confirm actual tier limits with Safaricom for your shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2b.max-amount
properties.description: Maximum KES amount accepted for a single B2B payment. Confirm actual tier limits with Safaricom for your shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.c2b.shortcode
properties.description: M-Pesa business shortcode that C2B validation/confirmation URLs are registered against.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.c2b.response-type
properties.description: Default action Safaricom takes if the validation URL is unreachable: 'Completed' auto-accepts the payment, 'Cancelled' rejects it.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.c2b.validation-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls before completing a C2B payment, allowing the transaction to be accepted or rejected. Requires validation to be enabled on the shortcode via Safaricom support.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.c2b.confirmation-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs completed C2B payment details to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.express-checkout.receiver-shortcode
properties.description: M-Pesa till shortcode being paid via B2B Express Checkout (USSD Push to Till). No initiator/security-credential needed — authenticated via the normal OAuth bearer token.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.express-checkout.partner-name
properties.description: Partner/organization name displayed to the merchant in the USSD PIN prompt during B2B Express Checkout.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.express-checkout.callback-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the B2B Express Checkout result to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-top-up.initiator-name
properties.description: M-Pesa API operator username used to top up a B2C shortcode's utility account from the working/MMF account (CommandID BusinessPayToBulk).

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-top-up.initiator-password
properties.description: Plaintext M-Pesa API operator password. RSA-encrypted at runtime using mpesa.daraja.certificate-path via MpesaSecurityCredentialService — never sent to Safaricom directly, and no separate security-credential property is needed.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-top-up.party-a
properties.description: M-Pesa B2C shortcode whose utility account is being topped up.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-top-up.queue-timeout-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls if the Account Top Up request times out in the queue.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-top-up.result-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the final Account Top Up result to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.transaction-status.initiator-name
properties.description: M-Pesa API operator username used to query the status of a prior transaction. Not yet wired to a service — reserved for automatic reconciliation of stuck B2C/B2B disbursements.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.transaction-status.initiator-password
properties.description: Plaintext M-Pesa API operator password. RSA-encrypted at runtime using mpesa.daraja.certificate-path via MpesaSecurityCredentialService — never sent to Safaricom directly, and no separate security-credential property is needed.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.transaction-status.party-a
properties.description: Shortcode or MSISDN that the transaction being queried belongs to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.transaction-status.identifier-type
properties.description: Type of organization receiving the transaction being queried. 1 = MSISDN, 2 = Till Number, 4 = Shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.transaction-status.queue-timeout-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls if the Transaction Status request times out in the queue.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.transaction-status.result-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the Transaction Status query result to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-balance.initiator-name
properties.description: M-Pesa API operator username used to query Working (MMF), Utility, and Charges Paid account balances for our own shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-balance.initiator-password
properties.description: Plaintext M-Pesa API operator password. RSA-encrypted at runtime using mpesa.daraja.certificate-path via MpesaSecurityCredentialService — never sent to Safaricom directly, and no separate security-credential property is needed.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-balance.party-a
properties.description: M-Pesa shortcode whose account balance is being queried.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-balance.identifier-type
properties.description: Type of organization whose balance is being queried. 1 = MSISDN, 2 = Till Number, 4 = Shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-balance.queue-timeout-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls if the Account Balance request times out in the queue.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.account-balance.result-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the Account Balance query result to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.reversal.initiator-name
properties.description: M-Pesa API operator username used to reverse a completed C2B transaction. Note: B2C payouts cannot be reversed via API — portal only.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.reversal.initiator-password
properties.description: Plaintext M-Pesa API operator password. RSA-encrypted at runtime using mpesa.daraja.certificate-path via MpesaSecurityCredentialService — never sent to Safaricom directly, and no separate security-credential property is needed.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.reversal.receiver-party
properties.description: M-Pesa shortcode that will be debited to refund the customer in a reversal.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.reversal.receiver-identifier-type
properties.description: Type of organization identified by receiver-party for a reversal. Must be 11 per Safaricom's spec.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.reversal.queue-timeout-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls if the Reversal request times out in the queue.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.reversal.result-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the final Reversal result to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2-pochi.initiator-name
properties.description: M-Pesa API operator username used to pay directly into a customer's Pochi la Biashara business wallet. Requires a B2C shortcode capable of both receiving and disbursing.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2-pochi.initiator-password
properties.description: Plaintext M-Pesa API operator password. RSA-encrypted at runtime using mpesa.daraja.certificate-path via MpesaSecurityCredentialService — never sent to Safaricom directly, and no separate security-credential property is needed.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2-pochi.party-a
properties.description: M-Pesa organization shortcode that money is disbursed from in B2Pochi transactions.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2-pochi.queue-timeout-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom calls if the B2Pochi request times out in the queue.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2-pochi.result-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs the final B2Pochi transaction result to.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2-pochi.min-amount
properties.description: Minimum KES amount accepted for a single B2Pochi payment. Confirm actual tier limits with Safaricom for your shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.b2-pochi.max-amount
properties.description: Maximum KES amount accepted for a single B2Pochi payment. Confirm actual tier limits with Safaricom for your shortcode.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.pull-transactions.shortcode
properties.description: M-Pesa organization shortcode whose C2B transactions are being pulled for reconciliation.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.pull-transactions.nominated-number
properties.description: The Safaricom MSISDN tied to this shortcode's KYC, found on the M-PESA portal — not something you choose arbitrarily. Required for the Pull Transactions API.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.pull-transactions.callback-url
properties.description: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL Safaricom POSTs pulled transaction batches to. Unlike every other operational M-Pesa API above, Pull Transactions needs NO initiator name/password/SecurityCredential — just the OAuth bearer token, same as STK Push and C2B Register URL.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.pull-transactions.pull-days
properties.description: Default lookback window (in days) when a query doesn't specify its own dates. Maximum of 2, since Safaricom only retains 48 hours of pullable transaction data.

properties.name: mpesa.daraja.pull-transactions.offset-value
properties.description: Number of records to skip in the pull transactions result set, used for pagination.

properties.name: stripe.secret-key
properties.description: Stripe secret API key (sk_test_* for sandbox, sk_live_* for production). Found in the Stripe Dashboard under Developers → API keys.

properties.name: stripe.webhook-secret
properties.description: Stripe platform webhook signing secret (whsec_*) — verifies /payments/stripe/webhook (deposits, saved cards). Found in Stripe Dashboard → Webhooks → your platform endpoint → Signing secret. Distinct from stripe.connect.webhook-secret below, which is a separate destination for events on connected accounts.

properties.name: stripe.connect.refresh-url
properties.description: Frontend URL Stripe redirects the user to if their Connect onboarding link expired, was already used, or is otherwise invalid. The frontend should request a fresh link (POST /wallet/stripe/connect/link) and redirect again from there.

properties.name: stripe.connect.return-url
properties.description: Frontend URL Stripe redirects the user to after finishing or exiting Connect onboarding. Reaching this URL does not guarantee onboarding fully succeeded — the frontend should call POST /wallet/stripe/connect/refresh or GET /wallet/stripe/connect/account to confirm actual status.

properties.name: stripe.connect.webhook-secret
properties.description: Stripe Connect webhook signing secret (whsec_*) — verifies /payments/stripe/connect/webhook (account.updated, payout.paid, payout.failed on connected accounts). Created as a SEPARATE destination from stripe.webhook-secret above via Dashboard → Webhooks → new destination → 'Listen to events on Connected accounts' — Stripe does not deliver connected-account events to the platform webhook's destination.

properties.name: paypal.client-id
properties.description: PayPal REST API client ID. Found in the PayPal Developer Dashboard under your app credentials.

properties.name: paypal.client-secret
properties.description: PayPal REST API client secret. Found in the PayPal Developer Dashboard under your app credentials.

properties.name: paypal.environment
properties.description: PayPal environment to target: 'sandbox' for testing, 'production' for live.

properties.name: paypal.webhook-id
properties.description: PayPal Webhook ID from the Developer Dashboard, used to verify that incoming /payments/paypal/webhook requests genuinely came from PayPal (see PaypalService.verifyWebhookSignature). Register your endpoint (https://<your-domain>/payments/paypal/webhook) under your app's Webhooks section to obtain this. If left blank, webhook verification fails closed and all incoming PayPal webhooks are rejected.

properties.name: paypal.return-url
properties.description: URL PayPal redirects the customer to after approving an order that requires a separate approval step (no saved/vaulted payment source, or a saved source that needs re-authorization).

properties.name: paypal.cancel-url
properties.description: URL PayPal redirects the customer to if they cancel out of order approval instead of completing it.

properties.name: flutterwave.client-id
properties.description: Flutterwave v4 OAuth2 client_credentials client ID. Replaces v3's static Secret Key/Public Key model entirely — v4 has no 'public key'. Found in the Flutterwave Dashboard under API keys.

properties.name: flutterwave.client-secret
properties.description: Flutterwave v4 OAuth2 client_credentials client secret, used with flutterwave.client-id to obtain access tokens from the OAuth2 token endpoint (see FlutterwaveService.getAccessToken).

properties.name: flutterwave.encryption-key
properties.description: Flutterwave encryption key, found in the Flutterwave Dashboard alongside your API keys.

properties.name: flutterwave.environment
properties.description: Flutterwave environment to target: 'sandbox' or 'production'. Unlike v3, this DOES determine the base URL (see FlutterwaveConfig.baseUrl()) — sandbox and production are genuinely different hosts, not just different key prefixes on one URL.

properties.name: flutterwave.webhook-secret-hash
properties.description: Arbitrary shared-secret string configured in the Flutterwave Dashboard (Settings → Webhooks → Secret Hash). Used as the HMAC-SHA256 key to verify the 'flutterwave-signature' header on incoming /payments/flutterwave/webhook requests (see FlutterwaveService.verifyWebhookSignature) — NOT a plain string comparison the way v3's 'verif-hash' worked.

properties.name: flutterwave.redirect-url
properties.description: URL Flutterwave redirects the customer to after completing a charge's authorization step (3DS, mobile money approval, etc.).

properties.name: flutterwave.sandbox-scenario-key
properties.description: SANDBOX TESTING ONLY. When set, every write call to Flutterwave carries this value as the 'X-Scenario-Key' header, forcing a deterministic mock outcome (e.g. 'scenario:successful', 'scenario:failed', 'scenario:auth_redirect') instead of default sandbox behavior. Leave unset in production — sending this against the live API is rejected or ignored depending on endpoint, and its presence in production config is a signal something is misconfigured.

properties.name: flutterwave.transfer.min-amount
properties.description: Minimum amount accepted for a single Flutterwave transfer (bank or mobile money disbursement). Confirm actual tier limits with Flutterwave for your account.

properties.name: flutterwave.transfer.max-amount
properties.description: Maximum amount accepted for a single Flutterwave transfer (bank or mobile money disbursement). Confirm actual tier limits with Flutterwave for your account.

properties.name: flutterwave.transfer.source-currency
properties.description: The currency your Flutterwave balance actually holds — used as payment_instruction.source_currency on every payout. NOT automatically the same as the destination currency the recipient receives in. Confirm your actual settlement/balance currency in the Flutterwave dashboard before relying on this in production.

properties.name: nowpayments.base-url
properties.description: NOWPayments API host. Sandbox and production are genuinely separate hosts with separate accounts/keys, not just different key prefixes on one URL — 'https://api-sandbox.nowpayments.io' for testing, 'https://api.nowpayments.io' for production. No trailing slash.

properties.name: nowpayments.api-key
properties.description: NOWPayments API key, sent as the 'x-api-key' header on every request. Found in Dashboard → Settings → Payments → API keys. Requires at least one wallet added under Payout wallets before a key can be generated.

properties.name: nowpayments.ipn-secret
properties.description: Verifies the 'x-nowpayments-sig' header on incoming IPN webhooks (see NowPaymentsService.verifyIpnSignature) — HMAC-SHA512 over the recursively-key-sorted JSON body. Found in Dashboard → Settings → Payments → Instant payment notifications. NOT the same value as nowpayments.api-key above, and NOT interchangeable between sandbox/production.

properties.name: nowpayments.callback-url
properties.description: Your own public HTTPS URL for /payments/nowpayments/webhook, sent as ipn_callback_url on every Create Payment request. No sandbox tunnel/CLI tooling exists here the way Stripe CLI's 'stripe listen' does — this needs to be a real reachable URL (e.g. via zrok/ngrok in dev) even while testing in sandbox.

properties.name: nowpayments.payout-email
properties.description: Your NOWPayments DASHBOARD LOGIN email — NOT the same thing as nowpayments.api-key, and a meaningfully more sensitive secret. Required only for payouts: obtains a short-lived JWT via POST /v1/auth (see NowPaymentsService.getAuthToken), needed in addition to the x-api-key header every other call uses. Deposits never touch this.

properties.name: nowpayments.payout-password
properties.description: Your NOWPayments DASHBOARD LOGIN password — paired with nowpayments.payout-email above for the same POST /v1/auth call. Treat this with real secrets-management discipline, more so than a typical API key — whoever holds it can log into the dashboard directly, not just make scoped API calls.

properties.name: commission.internal-transfer-rate
properties.description: Commission rate taken on internal wallet-to-wallet transfers (POST /wallet/transfer, POST /internal/transfer) — a decimal fraction, e.g. 0.01 for 1%, not 1. Expected lower than commission.gateway-rate, matching real payment-processing economics (an internal transfer costs nothing external, unlike a gateway withdrawal).

properties.name: commission.gateway-rate
properties.description: Commission rate taken on gateway-bound disbursements (M-Pesa B2C/B2Pochi, PayPal, Stripe, Flutterwave, NOWPayments) — a decimal fraction, e.g. 0.03 for 3%, not 3. Expected higher than commission.internal-transfer-rate, roughly in line with typical real-world gateway processing fees.

properties.name: frontend.url
properties.description: Frontend application URL used for CORS allowed-origins configuration.

properties.name: notifications.b2b-recipients
properties.description: Comma-separated admin/finance email addresses notified on every B2B success/failure (see MpesaDisbursementService.notifyB2BRecipients). B2B never touches a customer wallet, so there's no wallet owner's email to notify the way B2C/B2Pochi have — this is who gets it instead. Whitespace around commas is trimmed. Left empty/unset is safe: logs a warning and sends no email, never throws.

properties.name: exchange-rate.refresh-interval-ms
properties.description: How often (in milliseconds) ExchangeRateService re-imports every rate for the base currency from Frankfurter and re-fetches any other previously-saved pair, overwriting the stored MongoDB rows and refreshing the Redis cache. The same refresh also runs once on every application start. Read directly by the @Scheduled annotation itself via this same property placeholder, not through a properties class at annotation-processing time; kept in sync with the same default (10 minutes) regardless.

properties.name: exchange-rate.base-currency
properties.description: Currency whose full rate table (every quote Frankfurter supports) is bulk-imported on startup and on every scheduled refresh. USD is the wallet's ground-truth currency.

properties.name: exchange-rate.max-retries
properties.description: Maximum retry attempts ExchangeRateService's scheduled refresh makes per currency pair before giving up on that pair for the current refresh cycle and moving on to the next.

properties.name: commercial.enabled
properties.description: Master switch for the commercial (payment service provider) API under /internal/commercial/v1/**. When false the commercial endpoints are not served. Only the future Developer Service calls this API.

properties.name: commercial.serves
properties.description: Which environments this deployment accepts: 'live', 'sandbox' or 'both'. Production should run one deployment per environment, each with its own database and provider credentials. 'both' is meant for local development.

properties.name: commercial.currencies
properties.description: Currencies the commercial API accepts for payments and payouts, as upper-case ISO 4217 codes. Amounts are held internally in USD cents.

properties.name: commercial.quote-ttl-seconds
properties.description: How long a payout quote stays valid, in seconds. A payout that references an expired quote is rejected.

properties.name: commercial.signing.enabled
properties.description: When true, every commercial request must carry X-Timestamp and X-Signature (HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp, method, path with query, and the SHA-256 hex of the body). Keep false until the Developer Service signs its calls.

properties.name: commercial.signing.secrets
properties.description: Signing secrets accepted for request verification. List more than one during rotation so the old and new secret both verify. Blank entries are ignored.

properties.name: commercial.signing.replay-window-seconds
properties.description: Maximum allowed difference, in seconds, between X-Timestamp and the server clock before a signed request is rejected as a replay.

properties.name: commercial.events.developer-service-url
properties.description: Base URL of the Developer Service. Events are forwarded to POST {url}/internal/events and callback registrations are verified through POST {url}/internal/callbacks/verify. When unset, events stay in the outbox and are not forwarded, and live callback registrations cannot be verified. The developer service does not accept events or callback verification yet (a later slice adds them), so leave this empty until it does.

properties.name: commercial.events.api-key
properties.description: Shared secret sent as X-API-Key on calls from this service to the Developer Service. Must match the key the Developer Service expects.

properties.name: commercial.events.signing-secret
properties.description: Secret used to sign forwarded events. The signature is sent as X-Premisave-Signature: sha256=HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + '.' + body), with X-Premisave-Event-Id and X-Premisave-Timestamp alongside it.

properties.name: commercial.events.max-attempts
properties.description: Maximum forwarding attempts per event before it is marked failed. Retries use an increasing backoff.

properties.name: commercial.events.dispatch-batch-size
properties.description: Maximum number of due events the dispatcher picks up in one run.

properties.name: commercial.events.http-timeout-seconds
properties.description: Timeout, in seconds, for calls from this service to the Developer Service.

properties.name: commercial.events.dispatcher-enabled
properties.description: When false the scheduled dispatcher does not forward events. Events are still written to the outbox. Useful for running a second instance without double dispatch.

properties.name: commercial.events.dispatch-interval-ms
properties.description: How often, in milliseconds, the dispatcher looks for due outbox events. Read directly by the @Scheduled annotation through this property placeholder.

properties.name: commercial.sandbox.auto-resolve-delay-ms
properties.description: Delay, in milliseconds, before the simulated sandbox rail resolves a payment or payout to its final outcome. The outcome is chosen from the last digits of the amount in cents.

properties.name: commercial.sandbox.redirect-base
properties.description: Base URL used to build the redirect and checkout URLs returned by sandbox payments. The default is a non-routable placeholder host.

properties.name: commercial.registrations.max-per-app
properties.description: Maximum callback registrations per app and environment, counting every status.

properties.name: commercial.recovery-interval-ms
properties.description: How often, in milliseconds, the recovery sweeper re-applies ledger steps and holds that were interrupted part way. Read directly by the @Scheduled annotation through this property placeholder.

properties.name: commercial.expiry-interval-ms
properties.description: How often, in milliseconds, the expiry job times out stale pending payments, payouts and quotes. Read directly by the @Scheduled annotation through this property placeholder.

properties.name: commercial.mpesa.enabled
properties.description: Turns on the live M-Pesa rail of the commercial API: STK push payments and B2C payouts for live requests. Reuses the Daraja credentials under mpesa.daraja.*. When false, live mobile money requests return METHOD_UNAVAILABLE.

properties.name: commercial.mpesa.callback-base-url
properties.description: Public https address Safaricom can reach, with no trailing path, for example https://wallet.example.com. The rail appends its own callback paths under /payments/commercial/rail/. Required when the rail is enabled.

properties.name: commercial.mpesa.callback-secret
properties.description: Secret that signs the callback addresses given to Safaricom, so only genuine callbacks for a transaction are accepted. At least 16 characters. Required when the rail is enabled.

properties.name: commercial.mpesa.collection-max-kes
properties.description: Largest single M-Pesa payment, in whole KES. Safaricom's STK push limit is 250,000.

properties.name: commercial.mpesa.poll-after-seconds
properties.description: How long a payment waits for its callback before the status poller starts asking Safaricom about it.

properties.name: commercial.mpesa.poll-interval-ms
properties.description: How often, in milliseconds, the status poller runs. Read directly by the @Scheduled annotation through this property placeholder.

properties.name: commercial.mpesa.http-timeout-seconds
properties.description: Timeout, in seconds, for calls from the commercial M-Pesa rail to Safaricom.

properties.name: commercial.indexes.ensure
properties.description: Creates the indexes declared on the commercial documents when the service starts. Several guarantees depend on them, including unique idempotency keys and one ledger line per operation. Spring Data only does this itself when spring.data.mongodb.auto-index-creation is true.

properties.name: commercial.settlements.scheduler-enabled
properties.description: Turns the automatic settlement scheduler on or off. When off, merchants can still settle by hand; saved schedules simply do not run on this instance.

properties.name: commercial.settlements.scheduler-interval-ms
properties.description: How often, in milliseconds, saved settlement schedules are checked. Read directly by the @Scheduled annotation through this property placeholder.

properties.name: commercial.transfers.recovery-interval-ms
properties.description: How often, in milliseconds, transfers that were held but not completed are finished. Read directly by the @Scheduled annotation through this property placeholder.

properties.name: commercial.fees.collection
properties.description: Fee rules for incoming payments, keyed by method name (for example MOBILE_MONEY or CARD). Each rule has percent-bps (100 = 1%), flat-cents, min-cents and max-cents. A method without a rule uses the built-in default rule.

properties.name: commercial.fees.payout
properties.description: Fee rules for payouts, keyed by method name. Same rule shape as commercial.fees.collection. A method without a rule uses the built-in default rule.

properties.name: commercial.links.checkout-base-url
properties.description: Public address of the checkout page served by the developer service. A live payment link's url is this address plus /pay/{id}. When empty the url is the relative path /pay/{id}.

properties.name: commercial.links.sandbox-checkout-base-url
properties.description: Checkout address used in the url of sandbox payment links. Falls back to commercial.links.checkout-base-url.

properties.name: commercial.batches.items-per-run
properties.description: How many queued bulk payouts are sent to their rails on each dispatcher run. With the default interval of two seconds, ten per run is about five payouts a second.

properties.name: commercial.batches.dispatch-interval-ms
properties.description: How often, in milliseconds, the bulk payout dispatcher runs. Read directly by the @Scheduled annotation through this property placeholder.

properties.name: commercial.batches.dispatcher-enabled
properties.description: Turns the bulk payout dispatcher on or off for this instance. When off, queued payouts wait until an instance with it on picks them up, and finished batches are not completed.

properties.name: commercial.batches.stuck-after-minutes
properties.description: A bulk payout that was handed to a provider and has had no answer for this many minutes is closed as timed out and its money is released. Minimum 5.

properties.name: commercial.batches.max-items
properties.description: Most payouts accepted in one bulk request. Cannot be raised above 500.

properties.name: commercial.beneficiary.cache-hours
properties.description: How long, in hours, a provider's answer about a payout destination is reused for the same merchant before the provider is asked again. Between 1 and 168.

properties.name: commercial.refunds.approval-threshold-usd
properties.description: A refund above this amount in USD is returned with requiresApproval true. Until the approval workflow is decided the flag is informational and the refund still proceeds.

properties.name: commercial.refunds.recovery-interval-ms
properties.description: How often, in milliseconds, wallet credit refunds that were held but not completed (for example after a restart) are finished. Read directly by the @Scheduled annotation.

properties.name: commercial.disputes.evidence-window-days
properties.description: Days a merchant has to answer a dispute opened by the sandbox helper. Disputes raised by a provider carry the provider's own deadline.

properties.name: commercial.disputes.recovery-interval-ms
properties.description: How often, in milliseconds, disputes interrupted while opening or settling are finished. Read directly by the @Scheduled annotation.

properties.name: commercial.billing.scheduler-enabled
properties.description: Runs subscription billing: bills periods that have ended, retries failed invoices, finishes stalled attempts, resumes paused subscriptions and sends invoice.upcoming. Read directly by the @ConditionalOnProperty annotation.

properties.name: commercial.billing.scheduler-interval-ms
properties.description: How often, in milliseconds, the billing scheduler runs. Read directly by the @Scheduled annotation.

properties.name: commercial.billing.upcoming-days
properties.description: How many days before a billing date the invoice.upcoming event is sent. Allowed range 1 to 30; other values use the default.

properties.name: commercial.billing.stuck-minutes
properties.description: Minutes a collection attempt may sit unresolved before the recovery sweep looks at it. Must stay above the 5 minutes an Idempotency-Key is held while its request runs; values below 6 use the default.

properties.name: commercial.billing.batch-size
properties.description: The most subscriptions, invoices or notices handled in each step of one scheduler run. Allowed range 1 to 1000; other values use the default.

properties.name: commercial.billing.clock-wait-ms
properties.description: Sandbox advance-clock helper: milliseconds to wait for each payment to settle before stopping and asking the caller to call again. Allowed range 0 to 30000.

properties.name: commercial.rails.http-timeout-seconds
properties.description: Seconds the live rails wait for a provider to answer. Allowed range 3 to 60; other values use the default.

properties.name: commercial.rails.polling.enabled
properties.description: Looks open payments, payouts and refunds up with their provider, and finishes pending payment methods, so a lost or late webhook is picked up. Read directly by the @ConditionalOnProperty annotation.

properties.name: commercial.rails.polling.interval-ms
properties.description: How often, in milliseconds, open transactions are looked up. Read directly by the @Scheduled annotation.

properties.name: commercial.rails.polling.after-seconds
properties.description: Seconds a transaction must be open before it is first looked up with its provider. Allowed range 0 to 3600.

properties.name: commercial.rails.polling.batch-size
properties.description: The most transactions looked up per run per rail. Allowed range 1 to 500.

properties.name: commercial.rails.stripe.enabled
properties.description: Turns on the live Stripe card rail. Needs the wallet service's stripe.* credentials.

properties.name: commercial.rails.stripe.publishable-key
properties.description: Stripe publishable key returned to the customer's browser with a card payment.

properties.name: commercial.rails.stripe.webhook-secret
properties.description: Signing secret of the commercial webhook destination in the Stripe Dashboard (endpoint /payments/commercial/rail/webhook/stripe). At least 16 characters; without it results are found by polling only.

properties.name: commercial.rails.stripe.currencies
properties.description: Currencies card payments are taken in. They must also be listed in commercial.currencies.

properties.name: commercial.rails.stripe.min-usd-cents
properties.description: Smallest card payment in USD cents.

properties.name: commercial.rails.stripe.max-usd-cents
properties.description: Largest card payment in USD cents.

properties.name: commercial.rails.stripe.webhook-tolerance-seconds
properties.description: How far a webhook timestamp may differ from now before it is refused as a replay. Allowed range 30 to 3600.

properties.name: commercial.rails.stripe.setup-timeout-hours
properties.description: Hours a customer has to finish saving a card before the pending method is failed. Allowed range 1 to 720.

properties.name: commercial.rails.paypal.enabled
properties.description: Turns on the live PayPal rail (payments, refunds, payouts and saved accounts). Needs the wallet service's paypal.* credentials.

properties.name: commercial.rails.paypal.currencies
properties.description: Currencies PayPal payments are taken in. They must also be listed in commercial.currencies.

properties.name: commercial.rails.paypal.min-usd-cents
properties.description: Smallest PayPal payment in USD cents.

properties.name: commercial.rails.paypal.max-usd-cents
properties.description: Largest PayPal payment in USD cents.

properties.name: commercial.rails.paypal.setup-timeout-hours
properties.description: Hours a customer has to approve a PayPal billing agreement before the pending method is failed. Allowed range 1 to 720.

properties.name: commercial.rails.flutterwave.enabled
properties.description: Turns on the live Flutterwave rail (mobile money outside Kenya, bank and mobile money payouts). Needs the wallet service's flutterwave.* credentials.

properties.name: commercial.rails.flutterwave.mobile-money-currencies
properties.description: Local currencies mobile money is collected and paid out in. Kenya stays on the M-Pesa rail. They must also be listed in commercial.currencies.

properties.name: commercial.rails.flutterwave.bank-currencies
properties.description: Currencies bank payouts are sent in. They must also be listed in commercial.currencies.

properties.name: commercial.rails.flutterwave.source-currency
properties.description: Currency of the Flutterwave balance that transfers are paid from.

properties.name: commercial.rails.flutterwave.customer-email-domain
properties.description: Domain of the placeholder email used for a customer who gave only a phone number.

properties.name: commercial.rails.flutterwave.min-usd-cents
properties.description: Smallest Flutterwave payment or payout in USD cents.

properties.name: commercial.rails.flutterwave.max-usd-cents
properties.description: Largest Flutterwave payment or payout in USD cents.

properties.name: commercial.rails.nowpayments.enabled
properties.description: Turns on the live NOWPayments crypto collection rail. Needs the wallet service's nowpayments.* credentials.

properties.name: commercial.rails.nowpayments.default-pay-currency
properties.description: Coin a customer pays in when the request names none, in NOWPayments' own code.

properties.name: commercial.rails.nowpayments.min-usd-cents
properties.description: Smallest crypto payment in USD cents.

properties.name: commercial.rails.nowpayments.max-usd-cents
properties.description: Largest crypto payment in USD cents.

properties.name: commercial.rails.premisave.enabled
properties.description: Turns on Premisave wallets as a live payment method (the owner approves in the app, or under a standing approval for subscriptions) and as a payout destination.

properties.name: commercial.rails.premisave.consent-minutes
properties.description: Minutes a wallet owner has to approve a payment. Allowed range 1 to 1440.

properties.name: commercial.rails.premisave.mandate-max-usd-cents
properties.description: The largest single charge a standing approval for a subscription can be given, in USD cents.

properties.name: commercial.rails.premisave.mandate-hours
properties.description: Hours a wallet owner has to approve a standing approval. Allowed range 1 to 720.

properties.name: commercial.rails.premisave.min-usd-cents
properties.description: Smallest wallet payment in USD cents.

properties.name: commercial.rails.premisave.max-usd-cents
properties.description: Largest wallet payment in USD cents.

properties.name: commercial.c2b.enabled
properties.description: Turns on paybill payments by account reference. Needs commercial.mpesa.enabled as well. Read directly by the @ConditionalOnProperty annotations.

properties.name: commercial.c2b.shortcode
properties.description: The paybill customers pay (5 to 7 digits). Safaricom keeps one validation and confirmation address pair per paybill.

properties.name: commercial.c2b.response-type
properties.description: What Safaricom does with a payment when the validation address cannot be reached: Completed accepts it, Cancelled refuses it.

properties.name: commercial.c2b.merchant-validation
properties.description: Asks the merchant's registered VALIDATION callback before a payment is accepted.

properties.name: commercial.c2b.validation-deadline-ms
properties.description: Milliseconds the merchant has to answer a validation callback. Allowed range 500 to 10000.

properties.name: commercial.c2b.register-on-startup
properties.description: Registers the validation and confirmation addresses with Safaricom at start up. Otherwise call POST /internal/commercial/v1/c2b/register-urls once.

properties.name: commercial.c2b.reprocess-after-seconds
properties.description: Seconds a recorded but uncredited paybill payment waits before it is tried again. Allowed range 10 to 3600.

properties.name: commercial.c2b.sweep-interval-ms
properties.description: How often, in milliseconds, uncredited paybill payments are retried. Read directly by the @Scheduled annotation.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.enabled
properties.description: Creates an onboarding application for each new merchant and blocks switching production on without an approved application.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.required-documents
properties.description: Document types an application must hold before it can be submitted and have accepted before it can be approved.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.max-document-bytes
properties.description: Largest onboarding document in bytes. Values above 8388608 are lowered to 8388608 because documents travel as base64 inside a 12 MB request.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.max-documents
properties.description: The most documents one application can hold.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.staff-notify-emails
properties.description: Addresses told when an application is submitted or resubmitted. Empty sends nothing.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.mail-from
properties.description: Sender address of onboarding emails. Empty uses the mail account's own address.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.roles.review
properties.description: Staff roles that may start a review, add notes and mark documents.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.roles.return-for-correction
properties.description: Staff roles that may send an application back to the applicant.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.roles.approve
properties.description: Staff roles that may approve an application, which switches production on.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.roles.reject
properties.description: Staff roles that may reject an application.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.roles.reopen
properties.description: Staff roles that may bring a rejected application back into review.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.storage.mode
properties.description: Where onboarding documents are stored: LOCAL (the folder in path) or NETWORK (a folder on a share mounted at network.mount-path). Env: STORAGE_MODE.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.storage.path
properties.description: LOCAL mode folder for onboarding documents. It must exist and be writable by the service user. Empty refuses document uploads. Env: STORAGE_ROOT (the old COMMERCIAL_ONBOARDING_STORAGE_PATH is still read).

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.storage.network.protocol
properties.description: Kind of share mounted for NETWORK mode: SMB, NFS, SFTP, WEBDAV or OTHER. Env: STORAGE_NETWORK_PROTOCOL.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.storage.network.host
properties.description: Optional server name or address the mount must come from, as written in /etc/fstab. Env: STORAGE_NETWORK_HOST.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.storage.network.share
properties.description: Optional share or export name the mount must come from. Env: STORAGE_NETWORK_SHARE.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.storage.network.mount-path
properties.description: Local folder where the share is mounted by the operating system. Required in NETWORK mode. Env: STORAGE_NETWORK_MOUNT_PATH.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.storage.network.directory
properties.description: Sub folder on the share where documents go. Empty uses the root of the share. Env: STORAGE_NETWORK_DIRECTORY.

properties.name: commercial.onboarding.storage.network.require-mount
properties.description: Refuse reads and writes unless mount-path is really a mounted share, so a dropped VPN or NAS never sends documents to the local disk. Env: STORAGE_NETWORK_REQUIRE_MOUNT.
